items.title: Philippe Diallo learns harsh reality of mounting global challenge to Infantino
items.summary:
Philippe Diallo must be learning very quickly that the battle to wrest the Fifa presidency from Gianni Infantino takes no prisoners.
When Patrice Motsepe, the president of the Confederation of African Football (Caf), asked the presidents and general secretaries of its 54 member associations to give
items.text:
Philippe Diallo must be learning very quickly that the battle to wrest the Fifa presidency from Gianni Infantino takes no prisoners.
When Patrice Motsepe, the president of the Confederation of African Football (Caf), asked the presidents and general secretaries of its 54 member associations to give Infantino a standing ovation at Caf’s general assembly last weekend, Diallo, a guest at the event, had no choice but to cope with an uncomfortable moment.
“I have a report from all 54 associations that we are supporting Gianni,” Motsepe said of March’s election.
He took a more diplomatic, somewhat contradictory, tone when asked by the Guardian whether the African members of Fifa should consider which of Infantino, Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima would best serve the continent’s interests before taking an electoral position.
Diallo, the French Football Federation president, is of Senegalese origin through his father, and Motsepe said: “Diallo is our brother because of the connection. I sometimes say: ‘Why can’t they [Infantino’s opponents] get someone with no connection to Africa?’ It complicates my life. But I am also clear that it complicates things, in terms of the future.
“It is very easy for us now because we have a proven track record. This is Gianni’s last term, and Africa will be getting $25m [per association, over a four-year period from 2027]. The money is important, but it is also about his loyalty to Africa.”
Motsepe said he held talks with Diallo last Friday. “He came to see me and he engaged with me … We are absolutely clear, from an African perspective, that the interests of our confederation, to do what is in our best interests, are primary.”
Diallo was rather tight-lipped about his experience at the Caf congress, his first campaign foray outside Europe since he announced his candidature last week. He was not formally introduced to the Abuja congress as a Fifa presidential candidate nor given a chance to address its members.
“I came here to introduce myself to the federations and to observe things,” he said. “For now, I will not be speaking to the media. But I will have more to say in about three weeks.”
Infantino remains acutely aware that any chance of being elected to a controversial fourth term of office will depend on getting significant support in Africa. “Your support means the world to me,” he told the congress.
“If we are serious about saying that football belongs to everyone, everywhere, we have to fight for it. And I will fight for it … I like to speak with facts and not just with words … I remember that when I was first elected, each of you was receiving $250,000 per year from Fifa – $1m every four years. Now, 10 years later, you will receive $25m.”
The established view is that Infantino’s support base in Africa remains firm, but one member of the Fifa council – a supporter of Infantino, talking on condition of anonymity – takes a more considered position.
“It is easy to say that Diallo has no chance against Infantino, based on the cold reception that he got here,” he said. “But that will be very premature. Infantino got a similarly cold reception in 2016 when he came to Rwanda. None of the FAs wanted to speak to him. But he went on to win the election.
“No election is won or lost until ballots are cast. Every candidate will have to work very hard to win. No candidate can take this election for granted. Although there are three candidates in the race, I think that Tashima will eventually withdraw, and it will be a straight fight between Diallo and Infantino.”
One former member of the Caf executive committee, also speaking anonymously, thinks the court of arbitration for sport could decide Infantino’s fate before the election.
“The Fifa statutes (article 33 paragraph 2) allow only three elected terms for the president, and Infantino has served three terms,” he said. “The decision of the Fifa council not to count his first term of office because it was for three years and not four [as a result of Sepp Blatter’s resignation and the late Issa Hayatou serving as the interim president before Infantino was elected in March 2016] does not hold legal water … I expect that there is going to be a legal challenge, questioning the validity of his candidature. And there is a very good chance of that succeeding.”
That would be an interesting twist in the tale of Fifa presidential politics.

items.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
items.summary:
This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.
W
items.text:
This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.
Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.”
“Never any excuses, though,” adds Weah, who is critical of his performance against Turkey, his one and only start. “I went into the game overthinking a lot,” admits the 26-year-old. “When you’re overthinking, your feet stop working. It was rough for me. After the game I knew that’s not how I want to perform for my national team.” To date, that remains Weah’s most recent performance for the US.
If Weah is to earn a 54th cap for his country it will be under a new manager following Pochettino’s departure to Manchester United. The Marseille wide man does not believe the Argentinian’s absence will halt the momentum gathered by the US under his watch, regardless of who succeeds him. “He set the foundation and whoever comes in is going to ride that wave,” says Weah. “It’s an amazing group that they have and hopefully, they can continue levelling up and getting results against bigger opponents. The next goal for us is to win against top European sides and top South American sides.”
There is a degree of removal in the way Weah speaks about the national team. For now he is a supporter, a role he assumes without “disappointment” even though he craves a return to the fold. “I don’t want to force anything or beg,” he says. “I’m good where I’m at. If I end up back in the national team, and I don’t know when that will be, I’ll go. I’m focused 100% on club football.”
Weah’s route back in, as he acknowledges, is through his club form. He returned to Marseille from the World Cup understandably dejected but quickly had his spirits lifted by being named captain of the Ligue 1 side. “It’s an amazing feeling to be someone that’s looked upon as a leader, especially when it’s coming from the head coach [Bruno Génésio],” says the former Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain player. “I’ve worked super hard here and the fact that everyone sees me as someone that can lead the team and continue to lead the team is an amazing feeling.”
Génésio has said that Weah “incarnates what [he] wants from a captain,” highlighting his positive outlook and “irreproachable commitment”. His nomination, however, came within a difficult context: Pierre-Emile Højbjerg was stripped of the role by the club’s hierarchy – and against the will of Génésio – after he rejected a move to Newcastle United in the summer. The exit of Højbjerg, one of Marseille’s top earners, was seen as a means to alleviate the club’s financial concerns.
“In the summer, when they gave [the captaincy] to me, it wasn’t the best situation,” Weah admits. “I felt like it was appropriate to let Pierre still have that importance and that leadership … Pierre, for me, is still the main captain, and I let him still be vocal.”
Weah describes the “shared” leadership as a “wonderful thing” and insists that while he is undeniably more softly spoken than Højbjerg, his words retain the power to cut through. And he is particularly punchy when addressing the siege mentality at the club.
“A lot of the media wants Marseille to lose, 100%,” Weah says. “When we lose, everyone gets on us, and when we win, no one gives us credit. Marseille’s a hated club, and there’s nothing better than playing for a hated club when you win. I love being on the hated side of things because it gives you that drive, that want, that hunger to want to go and succeed and win things.”
Weah, son of former Liberian president and Ballon d’Or winner George Weah, speaks with poise and openness, not shying away from broaching political agendas on both sides of the Atlantic. “People need to speak more,” he says. “The younger generation needs to be able to exchange ideas with the older generation in order to come to common ground.” On the wider impact of the World Cup in the US, Weah says: “The beauty of seeing everyone enjoy it, the beauty of seeing everyone together smiling, whether you were from the States or whether you were from Bosnia or the Netherlands, we all came together and made it something beautiful. I think it definitely healed the world a bit in that moment.”
“There was a lot of noise, there was just too much going on,” Weah adds in regard to the Folarin Balogun affair. “I know about noise as well.”
It’s inescapable in Marseille. Angry, elated, never ambivalent sums up the fanbase in the working-class port city. With that comes a pressure that is hard to find elsewhere. “It’s a sink-or-swim environment,” says Weah in the auditorium of the club’s training centre, La Commanderie, which feels far removed from the bustling city below. “You have to be mentally prepared and mentally ready to be able to handle the rough days when they come and to be able to enjoy the good days. It can make or break you if you let it get into your head too much. The fans are very demanding. They’re spending their hard-earned money to come and watch us, and when we lose, it affects the city; and when we win, the city’s bumping.”

Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 201
items.text:
Dead hippo to be honoured on football club tifo
- Published
Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.
Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 2017, died on Thursday after swallowing a woollen hat that had slipped into her enclosure.
The Ohio side will now raise a banner depicting the nine-year-old semi-aquatic mammal in their post-season MLS Cup encounter with Nashville, who won the Supporters' Shield for being the highest-placed team in the league campaign.
Cincinnati said Fiona was a "beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world".
The tifo will be produced by fan group The Forge Cincy, who painted the display on Sunday in a garage next to Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.
The club will also make a donation in Fiona's memory for every fan in attendance to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden.
- Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says 
  - Published3 days ago
- Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo 
  - Published4 days ago
Cincinnati's Nick Hagglund, who hails from the city and is in his eighth season with the team, previously paid tribute to Fiona after scoring in his side's 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day of her death.
The defender yelled "that's for Fiona", mimicking the ears on top of her head, in a celebration video, external on the club's Instagram.
Later, on his Instagram account, external, Hagglund posted, "This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.
"Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call."
Cincinnati's tifo is one of a number of tributes paid to the hippo, with Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins wearing a Fiona sweater, external prior to his American football franchise's defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday.
Meanwhile handlers of the blue hippo balloon at New York's annual Macy's Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.
At birth Fiona weighed 13kg (29lb), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species, and previously inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.
Fiona swallowed the woollen hat around 10 days prior to her death, with the item getting into her enclosure by accident after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.
"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.
Hippos normally live up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.
Nashville finished top of the MLS Eastern Conference, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati.
However, having beaten Orlando in a one-off wildcard round, Cincinnati defeated Nashville 1-0 in the opening match of their best-of-three round one series.
Should Cincinnati win on Saturday they will progress to a one-off conference semi-final with either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC, with a conference final prior to the season-ending MLS Cup final.

items.summary:
Why Potts swapped West Ham for Club Brugge after 16 years

When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.
The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisc
items.text:
Why Potts swapped West Ham for Club Brugge after 16 years
- Published
When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.
The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisclosed fee.
And he has started every game, bar one missed through suspension, in all competitions.
After losing to Aston Villa in the Champions League, they have defeated Inter Milan, Lens and PSV.
"It really is a dream because you hear the music and then you see your family in the stands and you remember all the times that you watched Champions League on TV," Potts told BBC Radio 5 Live's Euro Leagues Show.
"You think of all the memories that you make watching it and to be playing in it now is something that every kid dreams of."
Potts' whole life had been based around West Ham. He had been with the club since the age of six and his father Steve, who made 506 appearances for the Hammers, is a first-team coach.
Potts Jr played 28 times for West Ham, with 25 of them coming last season as they were relegated from the Premier League.
He also had loan spells with Wycombe in League One and Portsmouth in the Championship.
"In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren't as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said 'let's explore options because this season I'm 22, turning 23'," Potts said.
"It's a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn't really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.
"I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.
"It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It's been the right decision for me and so far I'm enjoying it, I'm loving life here."
Club Brugge won the Belgian title last season and are second, just one point behind leaders Union Saint-Gilloise this campaign.
"It's a physical league," said Potts. "My running and physical stats have been higher than they've ever been. It's a demanding league in that way.
"Club Brugge demands a lot, from winning the ball back and going man for man in the press. And your responsibility off the ball is something that you have to take really seriously."
Potts says he has not started to learn French or Flemish and that team talks are done in English, with the side managed by Croat Ivan Leko.
And he revealed he has a lifelong history with the city.
"The whole move itself is funny because we used to visit Brugge when I was a kid," he said.
"We used to come around Christmas, so my family all know the city. And now I'm here they come out as much as they can.
"It's a great city with a lot of culture. It's brilliant. You won't find many places like it."
Next up for the side is the visit of Liverpool this week - with both clubs on nine points after four games.
The Reds are eighth and Club Brugge are ninth in the table.
"Everyone knows Liverpool as a club, the size and the Premier League teams," said Potts, who started for West Ham at home to the Reds last season.
"It's going to be a big game. We're level on points in the Champions League and we've put big performances in this competition and we're hoping that we're going to do the same."

But after a week when Arsenal publis
items.text:
Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his highly anticipated debut. But after a week when Arsenal published an article dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager.
Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match.
He was a stoppage-time substitute in Saturday’s win against Borussia Mönchengladbach, with Dortmund’s manager, Niko Kovac, saying Nwaneri faces a fight to get back in a team who lead Bayern Munich by two points and deploy the exciting Greece teenager Kosta Karetsas as one of two No 10s.
“We have some very good players in those attacking positions,” Kovac said before the Gladbach game. “The competition is fierce. He [Nwaneri] has played a lot of games and, at just 19 years of age, he will certainly play many more games for us.”
Nwaneri established that Premier League record in September 2022, at 15 years and 181 days old, but his real breakthrough came in the 2024-25 campaign as a replacement for the injured Bukayo Saka on the right. He scored eight goals, matching records set by Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen, and was even compared with Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, who was also born in 2007.
Nwaneri was rewarded with a new long-term contract despite strong interest from Chelsea and Dortmund, who have a record of signing emerging English talent. Heavy investment by Arsenal that summer, including Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke, meant he barely featured in the first half of last season and was allowed to join Marseille in January.
Arsenal chose the French club from a long list of suitors because they wanted him to develop under Roberto De Zerbi. Nwaneri scored on debut, but De Zerbi left by mutual consent a few weeks later and the attacking midfielder barely featured towards the end of the season.
The emergence of Dowman, who, as a 14-year-old, in December 2024, broke Nwaneri’s record as the youngest player to appear for Arsenal Under-21s, means he has slipped further down the pecking order. Mikel Arteta is understood to be keen for Nwaneri to develop as a No 10 rather than a winger and loaned him again despite not signing attacking reinforcements in the summer after the departures of Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus. Arsenal’s manager said on Monday he had been disappointed by Nwaneri’s fortunes in Germany.
“Because you go there and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn’t give you any advantage, so you need to earn it,” he said. “You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in such big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it’s extremely difficult. That’s the reality.
“You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that and it takes some time.”
While Nwaneri’s Arsenal career has stalled, he has seen his childhood friend Myles Lewis-Skelly begin to establish himself in his preferred central midfield role for club and country. The England Under-21s manager, Lee Carsley, remains a big fan, though, and Nwaneri repaid that faith by setting up the first two goals in a 3-2 win against France last week, even if Dowman took the headlines again by breaking Jude Bellingham’s record as their youngest goalscorer with a late winner.
Nwaneri, whose brother Emerson plays for ArsenalUnder-18s, was one of four training players called up for England’s World Cup preparation camp in Florida, with Rio Ngumoha, Josh King and Alex Scott, and remains on Thomas Tuchel’s radar. But as Arteta, who was sent on loan from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain at the start of his career, acknowledged when asked whether Arsenal may consider a January recall that it is up to Nwaneri to rediscover his best form at Dortmund.
“He was in Marseille as well. Marseille had a completely different context for a lot of things that I saw and expected to happen. But that builds a player, that builds the character and the career of a player. I’m so convinced of that.”
For Arteta, there is only one meaningful way for Nwaneri to deal with the frustration of his role as a substitute. “Try to change it for the one that you want,” he said. “That’s football.”

items.title: De Bruyne’s Napoli return will remind Manchester City what they are missing
items.summary: As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League t
items.text:
As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and the Champions League.
In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions.
De Bruyne left for nothing in the summer of 2025, but had fully returned the £55m City paid for him 10 years previously. Six Premier League titles, two FA Cups, five League Cups, a Club World Cup and that night in Istanbul when City conquered Inter, successes he will for ever cherish. Admittedly, the Belgian departed early that night in Turkey through injury, something he battled with in his later years in England.
Maresca was Guardiola’s assistant for the 2023 treble season, working closely with De Bruyne. “In the last 10 years, all the trophies the club achieved, Kevin was here and an important player, a fantastic player, a top guy, polite, fantastic,” he said. “It was a pleasure to work with him.”
His return may be made slightly more appealing because his powers have waned in Serie A and his teammates are not faring any better, although his compatriot Jérémy Doku said: “It’s fun to play with him. The quality he has is unbelievable, but we are all competitive so we all have to be on our best.”
At his peak, De Bruyne was the driving force for Guardiola, a two‑footed mercurial talent who could change a game in an instant. He was someone clearly more talented than most of the elite, able to glide past opponents, find a pass no one else could or just shift the ball from one foot to the other and smash in a goal from distance.
“I play more based on the feeling I have and where the space is, where I can feel I’m the most dangerous,” De Bruyne said on Monday. A reminder City do not possess someone of the same mould; even if Rayan Cherki may think he can be the heir, he is yet to consistently prove it.
“You always have to have courage to play football, you cannot only go long and just play for duels,” De Bruyne says of a style that evolved under Guardiola.
City have enjoyed these glorious talents for years; Yaya Touré could control a midfield, David Silva was able to control entire games. Maresca does not have access to someone like that and instead is attempting to create a unified team that makes the most of its expensive parts, but is yet to strike the perfect balance. For all of Erling Haaland’s incredible qualities as a striker, he cannot do it all by himself; he is reliant on service, something he is not getting from midfield or out wide.
Maresca tried the teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi alongside Elliot Anderson against Fulham on Saturday, leaving out the £125m summer signing Enzo Fernández.
Anderson was given a more attacking role, provided the sort of thrust De Bruyne often did. He does not possess the same technical expertise as the Belgian, although his volley may have earned a round of applause from his predecessor.
“It is not complicated, it is just a matter of knowing each other,” Maresca said. “I need to understand who is the ideal one for this kind of game and different kind of games. I don’t think it is just midfielders, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution.
“It’s part of the process. It is like a restart after 10 years with the same manager, same faces, same words, same methods. It’s not easy to change all of a sudden.”
Cherki is capable of amazing things, while Phil Foden infrequently threatens to rediscover his best form. De Bruyne, however, was part of a team that dominated. Often alongside Rodri and Ilkay Gündogan, the trio were almost the perfect balance of defensive diligence and attacking expertise, leaving opponents facing an nigh-on impossible task.
It is likely Maresca will change things for Napoli’s visit, with the ambition of a fourth win from five games in the Champions League, as City seek to secure progression as early as possible. Whichever team is put out, it will not have a talent like De Bruyne, meaning Maresca will have to work even harder to return to City’s Belgian-inspired peak.

Tuesday 24 November 2026 08:11, UK
The World Series of Darts will return to Dubai in 2027, with the Dubai Darts Masters set to be played for the first time in 10 years.
Dubai was one of the tour's original destinations and had previously hosted a World Series event between 2013 and 2017.
The World Series will kick off its 2027 season in Bahrain on January 15, before heading to the United Arab Emirates for the Dubai Darts Masters.

The tournament will see eight of the world's top PDC players battle it out in a 16-player knockout event between January 22 and 23 at the Coca-Cola Arena.
Scotland's Gary Anderson successfully defended his Dubai Darts Masters title when it was last held in 2017, beating Michael van Gerwen 11-7 in the final.
PDC chief executive Matt Porter said: "We're delighted to be taking the World Series of Darts back to Dubai.
"The city has a great history with the series, and Coca-Cola Arena will provide a brilliant setting for two days of top-class darts.
"We're looking forward to welcoming the world's best players and fans from across the region."
Eight first-round matches will be played on the opening night, before the knockout stages and the final are played on day two.
World Series ranking points will be up for grabs, as players look to secure their spots at the season-ending Finals in Amsterdam.
Ross Smith is out to defend his title after he thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals champion in September, winning his second PDC major.

items.title: Smith: I want to play on the PGA Tour
items.summary:
Cameron Smith plots pathway back to the PGA Tour after moving on from LIV Golf
Cameron Smith joined LIV Golf in 2022 after clinching his first major at The Open at St Andrews; the Australian will play select events on the DP World Tour in 2027; watch Smith in action at this week's BMW Australian PGA
items.text:
Cameron Smith plots pathway back to the PGA Tour after moving on from LIV Golf
Cameron Smith joined LIV Golf in 2022 after clinching his first major at The Open at St Andrews; the Australian will play select events on the DP World Tour in 2027; watch Smith in action at this week's BMW Australian PGA Championship live on Sky Sports
Tuesday 24 November 2026 07:49, UK
Cameron Smith has moved on from LIV Golf, is preparing for his invitation-only appearances on the DP World Tour and is already thinking about a return to the PGA Tour.
As the 2022 British Open champion prepared for the BMW Australian PGA Championship starting Thursday at The Lakes in Sydney, attention inevitably turned to his career goals and his steps toward a possible return to the PGA Tour.
"I guess that's the path. That's where I want to be now for sure," Smith told the Australian Associated Press.
"DP's given us a chance to kind of fulfil that. We'll see how that goes. There's plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it's going to be difficult.
"But for sure that's where I want to play."
How can Smith return to the PGA Tour?
Smith will not return as a full-time member on the DP World Tour, but is one of a number of former LIV players, including Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson, to sign an agreement with the tour to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments during the 2027 season, excluding Rolex Series events.
He receives an exemption to play this week, having won the BMW Australian PGA Championship three times in 2017, 2018 and 2022.
Under the DP World Tour and PGA Tour's current agreement, the top 10 players on the Race to Dubai Rankings qualify for the PGA Tour.
The number of PGA Tour cards available to players finishing at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings for the 2028 season is yet to be determined, with the PGA Tour set to launch its new two-tier championship structure the year after next.
However, to even have a chance at winning one of those coveted cards, Smith will need to play more tournaments on the DP World Tour's 2027 schedule.
He could do that by winning the co-sanctioned BMW Australian PGA Championship or the Australian Open at Kingston Heath, which begins on December 3 and also features Rory McIlroy.
"I think given what they've told me, I pretty much need to win this year to get membership," Smith said.
"It's all still very blurry to me at the moment. There are a lot of rules, but we'll have a few opportunities, and like I said, I've always managed to play pretty good down here, so why not start it off with a good one?"
The PGA Tour board last week said it had "thoughtful discussions" about the future of players at LIV Golf but otherwise seemed to be in no hurry to decide if there is room for them next season.
CEO Brian Rolapp said the Returning Member Program, which allowed Brooks Koepka to return to the PGA Tour at the beginning of 2026 with financial penalties, was not on the table.
Smith didn't take up that one-time offer in January, which applied only to players who'd won majors or The Players Championship from 2022 through 2025, which included himself, Koepka, Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau.
'It was a big move to go to LIV'
Smith is in a kind of limbo. LIV Golf, which lost the financial support of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and filed for bankruptcy on September 8, told a bankruptcy court earlier this month it had abandoned plans for a new version of the league and had begun winding down its business.
"There was a lot of uncertainty and then in a way it was good to just like get the noise over and done with," Smith, who joined LIV after winning The Open at St Andrews in 2022, said.
"It was a big move to go LIV at the start for sure, and I think everyone that was close to me and all my friends saw why I was doing it and why I made the decision."
Adam Scott said he had no doubts about Smith fitting back in.
"Cam's incredibly talented and he'll adjust to his new environment," Scott said. "He'll be just fine."

Wolves hit their stride, Stoke continue to dream but can they last the course and are QPR dark horses of Championship?
Wolves are improving defensively, Stoke look strong and QPR look resolute; Andy Hinchcliffe picks out the key stories in The Championship catch-up; a Sky Sports column focusing on t
items.text:
Wolves hit their stride, Stoke continue to dream but can they last the course and are QPR dark horses of Championship?
Wolves are improving defensively, Stoke look strong and QPR look resolute; Andy Hinchcliffe picks out the key stories in The Championship catch-up; a Sky Sports column focusing on the second tier.
Monday 23 November 2026 13:31, UK
Welcome to The Championship Catch-up, a new Sky Sports column in which Andy Hinchcliffe rounds up some of the key stories from the second tier. This week:
- Wolves are coming together under Peixoto
- Stoke look like they can last the course
- QPR's defensive improvements prove key
Wolves have added solidity at the back to attacking prowess
With the players Wolves have got and the way they play, they were always going to score goals. They've averaged around 1.7 goals per game across those periods, so they're still good for a goal under Cesar Peixoto.
But in the last seven games they've conceded only five, compared to the 14 goals they shipped in their first nine. They're not playing defensively, they're just defending well. They're keeping the ball and keeping teams away from their penalty area.
At the start of the season they were too open. They were great to watch and scoring goals, but conceding too many. They needed to find a balance. They didn't have to become ultra-defensive, but they did need some defensive strength.
- Transfer Centre LIVE! | Latest EFL news and rumours
- Championship table | Championship fixtures & results
They've got plenty of attacking threats. Raul Jimenez is still missing, but Adam Armstrong is doing really well and is a proven goalscorer at this level. They've got width, dynamism and options, while Andre plays a really important role sitting deep in midfield.
All I was looking for was more balanced performances. They didn't need to let the goals dry up just to keep clean sheets. They've managed to find that balance and do both. They're dominating games, keeping teams out and still scoring goals.
Even when they change the right-back, centre-half or left-back, they can maintain that defensive strength. They're clearly moving in the right direction and are now a much more balanced, complete team.
Kieran Trippier's experience has been invaluable. He cares about the club getting promoted back to the Premier League. Individually, he wants to do well, but he also wants the team to succeed.
He's perhaps not the player he was five years ago, but he can still have a huge effect. He'll have to get used to the fact that he might not play every game, but Wolves have the depth to manage that.
With Trippier, it's not just about his ability but also his leadership and experience. He can reinforce the standards they should be setting and what they're looking to achieve this season.

Can Stoke City last the course under Mark Robins?
Stoke City have won 10 of 16 games, more than any other Championship team. Would you have expected them to have won more games than Wolves, West Ham, Middlesbrough or Southampton after 16 matches? Probably not.
They're still overachieving in terms of the data, but Mark Robins spoke during the international break about the need to improve their performances. The league position doesn't really tell you how good you are. You have to monitor performances and look at how to develop and improve.
There's still work to do at both ends of the pitch, but they're getting goals from different players. George Hirst came in for big money and had been struggling for goals and not starting games. He won them the game against Birmingham, which is a lift for him and the team.
Against Birmingham, they were down to 10 men for a long time and showed the resilience to hold on to a 1-0 lead. When you look at everything, the foundations are there for them to get better.
How many experienced, very good coaches have gone to Stoke and not been able to make it work? We all hoped Mark Robins would succeed because of the work he did at Coventry, but there was always the question of whether he would become another coach who fell foul of a club where nobody seemed able to get things going.
I just think it's wonderful that it's him because he's such a brilliant coach. He's very understated and humble. I saw him after a game recently and asked him a couple of tactical questions. He was saying he was glad I'd noticed certain things he'd done. He's very engaging, but it's not all about him. It's about the job he's there to do.
Player for player, this Stoke side is better than last season's team. That's what I'm saying about their recruitment and the shape Mark is playing. They're better, and the fact they can improve further makes things look really positive.
But we're only 16 games into a long season. Mark will know winter is really tough for every team, particularly when you're up near the top and everyone is looking to knock you off your position. They'll be looking at their performances and adjusting their training because that's all you can do.
Could Stoke possibly be in the mix for a top-two finish? With the way they're playing and the players they've got, who could improve further, very possibly.
QPR have shown defensive improvements this season

Instead, the midfielder, who is widely regarded as
items.text:
Why has De Bruyne struggled at Napoli as he returns to Man City?
- Published
Kevin de Bruyne's move to Napoli in 2025 was supposed to mark a continuation of his glittering decade at Manchester City as he approaches the twilight years of his career.
Instead, the midfielder, who is widely regarded as one of the stand-out players of his generation, has seen his time in Naples threaten to turn sour amid an early injury, friction with his team-mates and rumours of a January exit.
Napoli were Serie A champions in 2024-25 - the year before De Bruyne's arrival - but are currently languishing in eighth, while they sit 27th in the Champions League after a heavy 4-1 defeat at Porto earlier this month.
Belgium international De Bruyne lifted 16 trophies in his 10 years at City and is guaranteed a generous ovation when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday but the highs of his time in England are in contrast to the struggles he is seemingly enduring in Italy.
"Not a lot I can say for the moment," said De Bruyne when asked about his future. "I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.
"There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening."
- De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change' 
  - Published10 hours ago
- Did Man City let De Bruyne leave too soon? 
  - Published14 October 2025
- Statue, Pep's tears & a missed sitter - De Bruyne's emotional farewell 
  - Published20 May 2025
'A bad show' in quarrel with team-mate
City decided not to renew De Bruyne's contract during the 2024-25 season and the player had the choice of heading to the US with Chicago Fire or staying in one of the top-five leagues in Europe.
The 35-year-old felt he could still cut it at the highest level but his first season at Napoli was heavily disrupted by a hamstring injury which kept him out for more than four months, restricting him to 21 appearances.
Napoli finished runners up to Inter Milan to lose their Serie A title and De Bruyne reportedly said, external he was "happy" manager Antonio Conte had departed in the summer as promises were not kept regarding the style of play.
But despite making his name as a technically gifted number 10, De Bruyne's role has been remodelled into a deeper holding one under Massimiliano Allegri in an ageing squad that has struggled this season.
In Porto, the fractures were clear to see, with De Bruyne having a heated on-field confrontation, external with striker Lorenzo Lucca and his team-mates were forced to step in to diffuse the situation.
The passionate side of De Bruyne's game was shown in Manchester too.
The midfielder shouted "shut up" at manager Pep Guardiola during a Champions League game against Real Madrid in 2023, and said "let me talk" when David Silva and Fernandinho were ushering him off the pitch at half-time shortly after he was booked against Napoli in 2017.
"Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli," Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino tells BBC Sport. "The point is that the whole team is having difficulties.
"We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.
"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show."
De Bruyne 'annoyed' by wife's misinterpreted quotes
De Bruyne has played 16 times for Napoli this season - contributing four goals and two assists - but his long-term future at the club remains unclear.
In September, De Bruyne's wife reportedly, external told a Belgian publication about their desire to move back home, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as the player leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.
Asked if the quotes had been misinterpreted, De Bruyne said: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she said.
"I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.
"Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family."
It has led to interest from the Netherlands with PSV Eindhoven making a £1.67m offer to sign him in January, but the two clubs are apart in their valuations as Napoli want up to £6.7m, according to Credendino.
"Napoli fans were not happy [with the interview]," he says. "There are many fans that say, 'OK, you can leave if you want, we are not putting chains on anybody'."
Napoli boss Allegri left the door open for a January exit by saying in his pre-match news conference the pair had "not spoken" about his future and it is "down to the players and who wants to leave" when the transfer window opens.
Maresca has fond memories of 'top guy' De Bruyne
City manager Enzo Maresca was assistant to Pep Guardiola during the 2022-23 campaign in which De Bruyne helped the club to a Treble of trophies and the Italian has fond memories of the "fantastic season" they spent together.
"No doubt, [he is] one of the best," Maresca said of De Bruyne in his pre-match news conference. "Not only personally but also for the history of this club. In the last 10 years all the trophies the club achieved Kevin was here.
"He was an important player, a top guy, polite and for me it was a pleasure to work with him."
This is not the first time De Bruyne will be facing his former club with a reunion with City in the Champions League last season.
That trip turned out to be a bitterly unhappy experience, with De

Two goals in 15 games - what's going on with Gyokeres?
- Published
A Premier League trophy and 21 goals in his debut season and a - on paper things have worked out perfectly for Viktor Gyokeres since his £64m transfer to Arsenal.
But, even with those achievements, it has been a tough start to the current campaign for the 28-year-old striker.
The Swede has started just one Premier League game this season and is yet to score in his eight league appearances.
He has started three games in the Champions League, two in the Carabao Cup, and has scored just twice in 15 games in all competitions. Not the numbers he would have hoped for after last season's glory.
It is not just this season that has seen Gyokeres suitability questioned for Arsenal though.
Even though he scored more than 20 goals in his first season in all competitions as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait for a title, his all-round game had its critics.
It has been near enough a straight battle for the number nine role between Kai Havertz and Gyokeres since the Swedish international signed.
And Gyokeres was thrust into leading the line for Arsenal quicker and more frequently than planned after injury kept Havertz out for long periods last season.
Although the Swede may be the more natural finisher, Havertz's all-round play is considered superior with the German also one of Arteta's most trusted players for big games.
Gyokeres, a "win-now signing", was bought for his ability to find the net but also for how he could open up spaces for his team-mates, something they have praised him for.
But playing with his back to goal and linking up play is not natural to Gyokeres and his failure to hold up the ball or win duels with centre-backs has led to fan frustration.
Arteta has spoken about how the striker has been working on improving his hold-up play and connections, and there were hints of it in the Champions League win over Slavia Prague where Gyokeres assisted the opener and scored the winner in arguably his best game of the season.
- Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious' 
  - Published15 hours ago
Why is Gyokeres not playing?
A big reason that Gyokeres is not starting games is that Havertz is fit.
Last season, Havertz suffered with knee and hamstring issues which meant Gyokeres was the only option Arteta had.
Had Havertz been fit, he would have played a lot more and the fact that he started the Champions League final and the key match away at Manchester City in last season's title race back this up.
This season Gyokeres has just six starts and Arteta says that his gametime and situation is similar to other members in the squad.
"We have rotated the team a lot and used the competitions as well to give minutes to players and exposure because they are all starters in my opinion," Arteta said.
"Viktor's case is one of many that they have been in the same situation where they play more in the Premier League or more in the Champions League which is not bad, eh?"
Arteta is open with his players about their standing in the squad and said that Gyokeres has not approached him directly about a lack of minutes.
"We have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing and to gather information about the way we are feeling and so far it has been very positive with Viktor and the rest of the team," he said.
The signing of Gyokeres is an interesting one in its own right.
The Arsenal recruitment team had done a lot of due diligence on signing, now Manchester United forward, Benjamin Sesko.
It is understood work on that deal had been done but a change of direction to sign Gyokeres happened after Andrea Berta became Arsenal sporting director.
Some around Arsenal have always thought that Gyokeres is not the usual forward that the Gunners would go for and his predicament of a lack of game time was always likely to happen, even if he did play a big part in them ending their trophy drought.
What do the stats show?
Gyokeres ended last season with 14 league goals but those strikes actually only won Arsenal two points on their way to winning the league.
That is because, although his penalty in the 1-0 win at Everton was the only goal of the game, Arsenal would have come away with a draw, so that strike factually only accounted for two points and not three.
But Gyokeres did put the Gunners ahead five times last season in the league which shows that, among the frustrating performances, he had plenty of impact.
Max Dowman stole the show with his goal in the 2-0 home win over Everton, when he became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, but it was Gyokeres' goal in the 89th-minute which put Arsenal ahead and although it did not lead to a point score on its own, it set them on the way.
Gyokeres also scored in the 4-1 north London derby win, putting Arsenal ahead when Kolo Muani had equalised after Eberechi Eze's opener.
It is unlikely that Gyokeres will be sold in January as he continues to get games in the Champions League and is a senior player who can score goals in big moments.
But if his lack of minutes in the league continue, Gyokeres, who is a driven and ambitious individual, will not want to be the player who is left out of the starting XI in the long term.
Additional reporting Chris Collinson, BBC Sport Football data analyst and Sami Mokbel senior football correspondent.

items.summary:

items.text:
tl;dr trynix.dev boots GUI programs now. Try solitaire, GL gears, xeyes, a voice, the weather over curl, or Firefox.
I remember watching the talk The Birth & Death of JavaScript by Gary Bernhardt and falling in love with the whimsical yet dreadfully serious unfolding of the story of how JavaScript will come to dominate all software.
Others have noted the inevitability of JavaScript’s dominance, so perhaps it was not surprising that Atwood’s Law holds true.
  Atwood’s LawAny application that can be written in JavaScript, will eventually be written in JavaScript. — Jeff Atwood, 2009
I highly recommend watching the talk if you have not already seen it, but the short and skinny is a lookback from 2035 and how JavaScript came to be the defacto language for all software.
In Bernhardt’s retelling of events, the date is worked back from 2035, however unsurprisingly, large language models have rapidly sped up the timeline. What was once perceived to be the end-state at 2035 has arrived years earlier and you can witness it unfolding at trynix.dev.
One of the most impressive creations I’ve managed to build leveraging nixpkgs-multiverse is https://trynix.dev.
It still baffles my mind that I can run any Nix package, over 300,000 distinct package versions, straight from my browser. Truly insane capability. I was however a little dismayed at the speed of the QEMU emulation in the browser. It was slow enough that the creation tipped more towards novelty than practicality.
I woke on November 20th and saw Domen Kožar sharing a single message in our TacoSprint Discord channel: unkernel.dev
It was the fast browser Linux experience I had sought to achieve, but with Nix.
  Aside What is unkernel? It is Linux compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the kernel and system components to run at wasm speed while only user programs are emulated. It was published by Pooya Parsa on November 19th, 2026.
In an AI induced manic frenzy, I adopted the new engine along with a slough of long-wished features almost immediately.
The proof is in the pudding: unkernel delivers remarkable speed improvements over qemu-wasm,11With a very healthy set of patches applied to make it even faster. especially on first runs where kernel work dominates. The new engine is able to deliver 2x to 32x faster performance depending on the workload.22The benchmark page tracks both engines over time, measured through the real page and shell.
JavaScript & WebAssembly nirvana.
Amazingly not only does the kernel boot quickly, it also enables networking, full-fledged graphical and audio experiences directly in the browser.
Windows. A program’s Wayland surfaces are composited in the page by wland, and they float over the terminal you started them from.
GL. The VM includes a minimal Mesa build with only the virgl driver, compiled to WebAssembly, rendering through your browser’s WebGL2.
Sound. The VM has an ALSA sound card, and can play audio through your browser.
Network. curl, git clone and pip install work. Each TCP connection goes over one WebSocket to a Wisp relay.33Thank you to @_pi0_ for adding trynix.dev to his Wisp relay allow-list. 
The best joke in Bernhardt’s talk is a browser running inside another browser: the Windows GIMP under Wine, in Chrome, in Firefox. Of course, I had to try it with trynix. 😈
Here is Firefox in trynix, and it loading trynix.dev, and then loading Firefox again inside itself.44Do not be too overjoyed. It took more than an hour for this to render.
Sit and bask in that insanity. That is Firefox, on Linux compiled to WebAssembly, in a Firefox tab, loading the site and then loading Firefox again inside itself. 🤯
2035 came early.

items.text:
115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting
- Published
Fifa president Gianni Infantino's globetrotting by private jet since his plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup can be revealed.
BBC Sport found Infantino has taken 39 private flights - the equivalent of one every three days - and visited 32 different countries since the news emerged on 28 July.
Our research found he travelled more than 102,800 air miles and spent just under nine days in the air in the space of 115 days.
Critics have accused of Infantino of using tools only at his disposal as president to aid his campaign for re-election next March.
They questioned whether his re-election campaign may have partly motivated any promises made or support offered during those visits.
Fifa said Infantino had a "statutory duty to maintain and develop good relations between and among Fifa, the confederations, 211 member associations, political bodies, and international organisations".
However, he visited nearly double the 18 countries he did in the same period in 2025.
The initial Times story that revealed Infantino's World Cup plan led to a wave of criticism around the world.
But, as BBC Sport revealed, many observers feel Infantino is now the favourite to be re-elected in the spring after his rivals struggled to find a candidate to run against him until the last moment.
And it appears Infantino has managed to shore up support around the world, with critics suggesting his globetrotting was a key part of that strategy.
There has also been concern about the environmental impact of his extensive travels.
Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - said Infantino's travelling was "part of his campaign".
He told BBC Sport: "The issue here is that Fifa does not have rules on campaign funding, so the president can claim that he's going there on official business when indirectly he's using that to campaign.
"And anyone else running against him very likely will not have the financial means to compete with that."
Infantino's position seemed vulnerable after it emerged he had been devising a plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, in a proposal called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).
Before FFE was abandoned, Infantino wrote to all 211 member associations saying they would receive $40m (£30m) if they backed the plan.
Lars-Christer Olsson - a former chief executive of Uefa - told BBC Sport the "important" question was "what does he promise and what are the conditions, as he already did when he promised cash if the members supported his FFE project?"
How did we track Infantino's flights?
BBC Sport gleaned the information about where Infantino had been travelling to, and when, from postings on his social media accounts.
The reasons for his travels include holding meetings with football association presidents, opening pitches, meeting politicians and attending confederation gatherings.
The private jets he used are operated by Qatar Executive (QE) - a subsidiary of the Qatar Airways Group, which is one of Fifa's sponsors.
BBC Sport used flight-tracking records and the jet registrations of the Qatar Executive fleet to compile a detailed log of Infantino's flights, totalling at least 39 since the start of August. Fifa did not dispute the figure.
It said "all travel is in line with Fifa's regulations" and there are "rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any Fifa official".
But Fifa declined to comment on how the use of QE flights impacts on the money available from the Qatar Airways sponsorship for the benefit of global football.
The governing body also declined to comment when asked when Infantino had last taken a commercial flight.
Olsson said: "What do these trips cost and who is paying, which are the implications for the total football community?
"Is he provided with transport in his private campaign with the idea of getting something back in return if he is elected? If Fifa is paying for private jets, would it not be better to invest this money in the member associations?"
Maduro said: "That's again a confusion between his role as president of Fifa and his role as candidate to Fifa presidency."
He said there were no regulations within Fifa on the "use of public money to support their campaign".
"There's no independent authority that controls that, there is no regulation of campaign funding," he said.
Infantino's trips included attending the Caribbean Football Union presidents' meeting and a junior football tournament in the Dominican Republic three weeks after FFE failed.
He then flew to Paris, where he attended the esports World Cup , alongside French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.
On his Instagram account, Infantino said he had "pledged Fifa's support" for the Pakistan Football Federation president's development plans when he met him in the US in September.
A few days later, he referenced a "wonderful discussion" with the president of the Latvian Football Federation during a visit to Riga, describing him as "my dear friend".
During a visit to Indonesia in October for the final of the Fifa ASEAN Cup, he met presidents from the football federations of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Philippines, Qatar, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste.
He said: "Having your support and shared passion on this momentous occasion means a great deal and together we will continue driving this game forward."
And during a recent trip to Manila, he performed on stage as part of a quartet called the 'Backache Boys', alongside officials from the Asian Football Confederation, and the football federations of Malaysia and the Philippines.
1 of 3
Concern over sustainability
Based on our log of Infantino's private-jet flights, we calculated he spent 213 hours and 49 minutes in the air, travelling about 102,870 air miles.

Drew Stevens kicks last-second field goal to lift Washington Commanders to surprise win over Joe Burrow's high-flying Cincinnati Bengals; watch an NFL Thanksgiving triple-header li
items.text:
NFL: Washington Commanders beat Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals in upset after last-second field goal from Drew Stevens
Drew Stevens kicks last-second field goal to lift Washington Commanders to surprise win over Joe Burrow's high-flying Cincinnati Bengals; watch an NFL Thanksgiving triple-header live on Sky Sports NFL from 5pm on ThursdaySky Sports
Tuesday 24 November 2026 06:34, UK
Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired as the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.
After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts.
Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight. The Commanders quarterback spiked it with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest.
Daniels finished with 283 yards passing, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and Stevens was five for five on field goals as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants.
- Recap on all the action, highlights and analysis from Week 11
- Who is NFL MVP favourite?
- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns for AFC North-leading Cincinnati (7-3), but the Commanders largely held in check a Bengals team that had won five straight, scoring 31 points or more each time.
Washington's defense forced Burrow to settle for checkdowns all night.
The dangerous Bengals receiving duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for just seven catches for 74 yards.
Washington coach Dan Quinn made another questionable late-game decision when he sent Stevens out on fourth-and-one to kick a 41-yard field goal with 2:26 left for a 19-17 lead. That left plenty of time for Burrow, who found Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard completion to move the Bengals into field goal range.
A sack pushed the Bengals back, but McPherson nailed the long kick with 46 seconds remaining.
The game got off to a slow start in rainy conditions but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter.
Burrow's four-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young put the Bengals ahead 17-10, and the Commanders rallied with three field goals by Stevens.
There was an unexpected stoppage early in the third when the stadium lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone. After a delay that lasted about four minutes, Stevens converted from 36 yards to tie the game at 10-all.
Washington held Cincinnati to three points on its first four drives before Higgins' 31-yard touchdown catch that made it 10-0.
Jacory Croskey-Merritt, activated off injured reserve earlier Monday, scored on a one-yard run for the Commanders with 12 seconds left before halftime.

Dalton Smith has had an outstanding 2026, winning and defending the WBC super-lightweight world title with wins over Subriel Matias and Alberto Puello; Smith believes he can headline at Hillsborough Stadium in his
items.text:
Dalton Smith: Paths align better for Shakur Stevenson unification than Adam Azim fight
Dalton Smith has had an outstanding 2026, winning and defending the WBC super-lightweight world title with wins over Subriel Matias and Alberto Puello; Smith believes he can headline at Hillsborough Stadium in his Sheffield hometown with American star Shakur Stevenson a potential opponent
Monday 23 November 2026 14:23, UK
Dalton Smith, the WBC super-lightweight champion, thinks he's more likely to fight Shakur Stevenson next than Adam Azim.
Sheffield's Smith has had an outstanding year, knocking out Subriel Matias in New York to win his world championship and defending the belt against Alberto Puello in his Sheffield hometown.
American star Shakur Stevenson secured the WBO's super-lightweight championship when he beat Teofimo Lopez in January.
Both Smith and Stevenson are looking for their next opponents and a unification between the pair would be an appealing match up.
"Boxing's business and if it makes good business on both sides it's definitely a fight that can be made. Obviously there's other champions, other belts. I just want to be part of the biggest fights," Smith told Sky Sports.
"It's a fight where the paths align a little bit better than me and Adam Azim right now. But like I said we'll see."
His advice to Azim is: "Be in world level fights.
"It's a fight what gets talked about a lot," Smith said of Azim. "I've got my own path I'm going on. I'm not just saying I'm doing. I think Adam needs to play his part as well.
"I'm not really concentrating on Adam. I'll let him do what he's doing.
"I'm concentrating on a big 2027 for me."
He would love to headline at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield next year.
"I'm in a position now to be part of some big, big fights," Smith said. "I'd love to have Hillsborough, I'd love to win more world titles.
"It's something I've dreamt of for years, I've always said it. People probably thought I was delusional at the time saying it, but I kept following the dream and I feel like it's very close. Possibly something we can get over the line next year. It'll just be big for Sheffield, big for the city and I'll be proud to say I've done it.
"I feel like I'm carrying that torch for the city now."

items.title: Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?
items.summary: We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain)
items.text:
We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.
So what has it done to the standings? Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.
UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 5
1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN (no change)
- Previous rank: 1
- Games since MD3: defeated Lyon 2-0; defeated Le Havre 5-1; defeated Villarreal 6-0; defeated Troyes 1-0; defeated Nice 3-2
- MD5 opponent: vs. AS Roma (Wednesday)
Would anyone bet against them winning it all a third straight time? Our voters were nearly unanimous -- 15 of 17 -- in crowning the French champions and back-to-back Champions League winners as the best team in this competition, but there are tough tests to come.
PSG continue to look sharp and ruthless domestically, which isn't normally their rhythm at this time of year. (Folks will remember that they generally wake up, form-wise, after Christmas, at least in recent seasons.) Ferran Torres keeps showing why he was such a savvy summer signing from Barcelona, chipping in eight goals and an assist as an occasional starter, with the likes of Senny Mayulu -- one of 12 players to get on the score sheet in Ligue 1 this season -- also stepping up to contribute in the attacking third.
They were managing without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in October and faces a lengthy spell on the sideline, but Saturday's season-ending knee injury suffered by Doué in this weekend's win over Nice will tax their reserves over the course of a grueling campaign. Up next is a potentially tricky midweek date with Roma who, despite losing to Man United in Matchday 4, have one of the stingiest defenses in Serie A (11 goals conceded in 12 games).
2. BARCELONA (no change)
- Previous rank: 2
- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Real Madrid; defeated Alaves 6-1; defeated Aston Villa 3-0; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-1; defeated Villarreal 3-2
- MD5 opponent: at Sabah FK (Wednesday)
The Spanish champions continue to be box-office entertainment every week. They simply do not believe in drawing games; every single one of their games this season has ended with a decisive winner and loser, with their back-to-back losses to PSG and Real Madrid surrounded by wins up and down the schedule. Since the Clasico setback it has largely been business as usual, with big wins over Alaves and Villa followed by a very different pair of comeback victories at Atletico and home to Villarreal. Sunday's win had the feel of a predator toying with its prospective dinner, as Villarreal scored twice in the opening seven minutes to daze Lamine Yamal & Co. early, only for the champs to respond with three goals in 10 second-half minutes and a three-point lead at the top of LaLiga.
Like PSG, they have a simmering injury concern to their defensive corps, with several front-line defenders in various stages of rehab or treatment: Andreas Christensen has managed just 30 minutes of game time since mid-September, Pau Cubarsí's health is being monitored after a hip injury on international duty, and Jules Koundé/Eric García are just coming back from absences of their own. Rodri's ongoing fitness is a worry too as the best choice to shield a vulnerable back line, but as long as they are scoring goals by the bucketload -- their 51 in 13 LaLiga games is more than the bottom four teams in the table combined -- it feels like a minor concern. That said, Hansi Flick's side will need to tighten up once we get into the business end of this competition.
3. ARSENAL (no change)
- Previous rank: 3
- Games since MD3: defeated Everton 2-0; lost 5-3 on penalties vs. Fleetwood Town (Carabao Cup); defeated Liverpool 1-0; defeated Slavia Prague 2-1; defeated Hull 1-0; drew 2-2 vs. Newcastle
- MD5 opponent: vs. Borussia Dortmund (Tuesday)
The Gunners already have a six-point lead atop the Premier League after just 11 games, which feels like business as usual for Mikel Arteta's side, but the manner in which they slumped to a draw at Newcastle on Saturday shows that this side isn't quite at the juggernaut levels it achieved last season. Their aggressive press yielded the opening goal, when Kai Havertz snagged the ball from Lewis Hall and teed up Eberechi Eze, but Noni Madueke whiffed before halftime to double their lead and Arsenal crumbled after the break, conceding twice. Noni Madueke eventually atoned by rifling in the equalizer, but the loss of control and absence of ruthlessness will have Arsenal's rivals on notice.
This week's visit of Dortmund has all the hallmarks of a trap game, considering BVB are having a superb season so far and Arteta will have one eye on next weekend's visit of Man City to the Emirates instead. Shrugging off Saturday's torpor and asserting dominance over Niko Kovac & Co. on Tuesday will be essential to demoralizing the chasing pack.
4. REAL MADRID (up 2)
- Previous rank: 6
- Games since MD3: defeated Barcelona 2-1; defeated Racing Santander 3-0; defeated AEK Athens 3-2; defeated Valencia 3-0; defeated Celta Vigo 2-1
- MD5 opponent: vs. PSV Eindhoven (Tuesday)
Since Jose Mourinho announced his return to the Bernabeu this summer, we've been wondering when things would start to come apart at the seams. items.summary:
S.9348A/A.10411A Prohibits Car Companies from Charging for Built-In Features
Amid Rising Consumer Fees, New Law Increases Price Transparency and Puts Money Back in New Yorkers’ Pockets
Governor Kathy Hochul today signed a bill restricting motor vehicle manufacturers and dealers from charging consume
items.text:
S.9348A/A.10411A Prohibits Car Companies from Charging for Built-In Features
Amid Rising Consumer Fees, New Law Increases Price Transparency and Puts Money Back in New Yorkers’ Pockets
Governor Kathy Hochul today signed a bill restricting motor vehicle manufacturers and dealers from charging consumers subscription fees after they purchase a vehicle. Amid rising consumer prices, the new law guards against a rising trend of car companies charging car owners fees to activate and use built-in features like heated seats, enhanced navigation, hands-free driving and entertainment options that do not present an ongoing expense for dealers and manufacturers.
“New Yorkers are already struggling with rising prices due to Trump’s affordability crisis, and we’re not going to let harmful business practices increase the cost of living even more,” Governor Hochul said. “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets.”
S.9348A/A.10411A prohibits motor vehicle manufacturers, dealers or third-party service providers from adding subscription services or charging post-purchase fees for any motor vehicle feature that uses pre-installed components or hardware that do not have an ongoing cost. As vehicles become more advanced, the new law aims to establish clear rules preventing exploitative practices and prevent post-purchase fees as a future automotive business model.
New York Attorney General Letitia James said, “No one should have to pay recurring fees just to use features in a car they already bought. My office has secured millions of dollars for New Yorkers throughout the state who were charged illegal junk fees when purchasing a car. Unfair fees are fueling rising costs, and I am proud to work with Governor Hochul and the legislature to bring costs down.”
State Senator James Skoufis said, “People ought to know they’re able to use their already-installed remote start or heated seats during the winter without a monthly subscription. This new law will simply and clearly prohibit car manufacturers from ripping off New Yorkers who already paid for vehicle features when they purchased their car. It’s a common sense law and I’m grateful for the Governor and Assemblymember Magnarelli for their partnership enacting this legislation."
Assemblymember William B. Magnarelli said, "I thank Governor Hochul for recognizing the importance of this legislation, particularly as technology continues to evolve at a rapid pace. This law will help protect New Yorkers from unfair fees and ensure consumers aren’t paying extra for features already built into their vehicles.”
The law will take effect in 90 days on February 27, 2027.
This new law is the latest in Governor Hochul’s ongoing commitment to help address the cost of living by putting money back in the pockets of New Yorkers statewide. Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, she has:
- Secured reforms to lower auto insurance premiums for New Yorkers, battling fraud, limiting damages paid out to bad actors, and ensuring consumers, not insurance companies, are prioritized.
- Signed legislation requiring businesses to notify consumers of upcoming renewals and price changes as well as provide clear instructions on how to cancel subscriptions.
- Cut middle-class taxes to their lowest rates in 70 years.
- Tripled the Child Tax Credit, providing families up to $1,000 per child under the age of four and up to $500 for school-aged children, beginning in 2026.
- Made school meals free for every student, saving families $1,600 per child every year.
- Sent Inflation Refund checks to 8.2 million New Yorkers — up to $200 for individuals and up to $400 for families.
- Increased the maximum weekly unemployment benefit by $300 a week.
