items.title: U.S. to co-host Women's World Cup in 2031; U.K. wins bid for 2035
items.summary:
The United States has been confirmed as co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, before the United Kingdom will host the tournament four years later.
The FIFA congress on Monday approved a joint bid from Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 World Cup.
The combined bid fr
items.text:
The United States has been confirmed as co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, before the United Kingdom will host the tournament four years later.
The FIFA congress on Monday approved a joint bid from Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 World Cup.
The combined bid from England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland was the sole bidder for the 2035 competition. To date, 19 venues have been put forward as potential options to host the tournament, with 14 grounds across England, two in Scotland, two in Wales and one in Northern Ireland.
The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments -- the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games -- and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.
"This will be the largest women's sporting event in history," the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body's headquarters in Zurich. "Which means we have to deliver."
The U.S.-led bid previously predicted tournament revenues of $4 billion, and Parlow Cone said after the FIFA decision that "if we do it right we probably will surpass that."
FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and host the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.
The U.S.-led 2031 project across the Concacaf regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.
Women's soccer in Jamaica already has a good reputation, with standout forward Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw starring for Manchester City and the national team finishing unbeaten above Brazil in their group at the 2023 World Cup.
Parlow Cone said "we have a responsibility to raise the boats of every country" in women's soccer.
"I know first hand what hosting a Women's World Cup can do, and I wanted the same for throughout our region. It's going to be transformative for us, but imagine what it will do for Jamaica for the 'Reggae Girlz' to play in their home stadium in a World Cup match," Parlow Cone said.
The pair of four-nation co-hosting bids had a clear run in the past 20 months and were approved Monday by acclamation in an online meeting of FIFA's 211 member federations.
The U.S. previously hosted the Women's World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003. The national team's tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles.
It will be the first time since 1966 the U.K. has hosted a World Cup. The U.K. will also host the men's European Championships in 2028, but had previously failed in bids to secure the 2006 and 2018 men's World Cups.
The English stadiums included in the bid are: Brighton's Amex, Bristol City's Ashton Gate, Nottingham Forest's City Ground, Leeds United's Elland Road, Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, Manchester City's Etihad Stadium, Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium, Manchester United's Old Trafford, Newcastle United's St James' Park, Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park, Sunderland's Stadium of Light, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Villa Park and Wembley.
Chelsea's potential new stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped ground and Birmingham's new 62,000-capacity Powerhouse Stadium could also be added.
In Wales, the Principality Stadium and Cardiff City Stadium are on the list. A redeveloped Windsor Park in Northern Ireland is also on the list as are Edinburgh's Easter Road and Glasgow's Hampden Park in Scotland.
FIFA's evaluation of the bid gave it a rating of 4.3 out of five, with the contractual framework of the bid rated "medium risk."
FIFA's evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.
"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.
"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with FIFA and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."
English FA chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the congress after the bid's success had been confirmed.
"Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035," Hewitt said.
"We're deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women's football on behalf of the global football family.
"As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women's World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.
"Together, we will celebrate the power of women's football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women's World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of."
- 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup: Format, who has qualified ahead of playoffs?
- England World Cup playoff squad: Isobel Goodwin and Katie Cox named
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women's sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.
"Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep -- and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle."

items.title: Houston says Herrera available for Dynamo playoff opener amid MLS probe
items.summary:
MLS is gathering information regarding the reported arrest of Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera for suspicion of driving while intoxicated ahead of the team's first game of the best-of-three round one series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24.
"Major League Soccer is aware of an i
items.text:
MLS is gathering information regarding the reported arrest of Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera for suspicion of driving while intoxicated ahead of the team's first game of the best-of-three round one series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24.
"Major League Soccer is aware of an incident involving Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera," MLS said in a statement to ESPN. "The League is gathering additional information and will refrain from further comment pending a review of the matter."
Houston Dynamo head coach Ben Olsen confirmed that as of Monday, Nov. 23, Herrera is eligible to feature in the playoff match against the Earthquakes.
Multiple reports said Herrera was charged with suspicion of DWI in Montgomery County, Texas, on Saturday. The Dynamo told ESPN on Sunday the club was aware of an incident involving Herrera.
"It's all in the league's hands. So far, he's available to play tomorrow," Olsen said in a press conference Monday.
Olsen added that Herrera's situation is not ideal, but does not present a distraction for the rest of the team ahead of the playoff match.
"The incident in question is Friday night, all right? And don't want to get into too many details. Is it ideal? No, but by and large, it's not a huge distraction. It's not ideal. But, you know, the group is a very healthy one, and we all have love for Hector, and when these things creep up, you deal with them in the right way, through process," Olsen added.
"It's been addressed, and it's been put to bed. The team is in a good place. This is not any excuse. Throughout the season, things like this happened, you know? And you, whether it's family members or, you know, things happen throughout seasons, and you address them, and you move on.
"And this isn't, again, the first thing that's happened this year, that we've had to address as a group, and all our focus right now is on trying to advance against a really good team, and I really don't even want to get into any more questions on Hector, frankly, because I think right now, the focus should be on our group, and the opportunity in front of us against San Jose."
Herrera previously faced MLS sanctions when he was sent off in 2024 for spitting on a referee. The Houston Dynamo chose to deny his 2025 contract extension following the incident, prior to re-signing Herrera in 2026.
The midfielder briefly featured for Liga MX side Toluca in 2025, before returning to MLS.
Herrera has recorded nine goals and 25 assists in 99 MLS regular season and playoff appearances for the Dynamo across four seasons. He played in 30 regular season games in 2026 since rejoining the club.
ESPN writer Cesar Hernandez contributed to this report.

items.title: Son Heung-Min: Thomas Müller spot-on about lack of pressure in MLS
items.summary:
LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.
Last week, Vancouver Whitecaps star Müller said it is difficult to compare the MLS to the Premi
items.text:
LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.
Last week, Vancouver Whitecaps star Müller said it is difficult to compare the MLS to the Premier League or other European leagues because "there is no relegation. There is no big pressure."
Son, who moved to the MLS in 2025 after a lengthy spell at Tottenham Hotspur, said Müller was "spot on" when asked about the German's remarks by reporters.
"The MLS is getting big, big name players are coming to the MLS but sometimes you feel there's less pressure because there isn't relegation.
"I can't control that but I'm enjoying this league...But I think Thomas was spot on. I thoroughly agree. He had an amazing career in the Bundesliga and he feels he's right to say it," the South Korea star said.
"I was in the Premier League -- every week, it's the biggest pressure. If you're not performing, if you're not playing well, if your team starts struggling or is in the bottom half of the table then you're having a difficult time.
"I think it makes it more fun. I want the best for the MLS, so maybe they can look into it and do something."
Müller, the most decorated German player of all time, sparked a conversation around the MLS' system of no promotion or relegation with his comments.
"[In Europe with relegation] The players have maybe no contracts for next year when you go down, so the playing style changes," the former Bayern Munich man said at the time. "When you play a bottom of the league team in Europe they fight for their lives. And sometimes I have the feeling, because of the [MLS] system, the playing style is a little bit more, let's say, optimistic, or careless, defensively.
- Philadelphia's Cavan Sullivan wins MLS Young Player of the Year award
- How B.J. Callaghan's long, winding coaching journey led to Nashville success
- Reports: Dynamo's Herrera charged with DWI, club aware of 'incident'
"So a little bit, just a little bit more, the French would say, laissez faire," he said. "That's maybe good for seeing some nice offensive plays when the games are opening up. When I compare it I see sometimes really, really good individual actions in players.
"What I miss sometimes is maybe the consistency, the good and the bad, the gap is bigger.
"[In MLS] There is, oh yeah, we do a rebuild," he said. "Nobody is happy to lose but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe yeah, you lose budget for the next year, the whole club. You lose people working at the club when the budget changes. It's totally different for fans."

items.title: Spirit fire González after losing NWSL Championship for 3rd straight season
items.summary:
The Washington Spirit have fired head coach Adrián González following the team's loss in Saturday's NWSL Championship, the team confirmed on Monday.
Washington's loss on Saturday marked the third straight season in which the team was defeated in the NWSL Championship.
González was the head coach of
items.text:
The Washington Spirit have fired head coach Adrián González following the team's loss in Saturday's NWSL Championship, the team confirmed on Monday.
Washington's loss on Saturday marked the third straight season in which the team was defeated in the NWSL Championship.
González was the head coach of the Spirit in the past two finals. He was an assistant to Jonathan Giráldez in 2024 after serving as acting head coach earlier that year.
"We are grateful to Adrián for his leadership and the success he has helped bring to the Spirit over the past three seasons," Spirit president of soccer operations Haley Carter said in a statement. "He has led the team with class and professionalism and made a lasting contribution to this club. As we plan for the Spirit's future, all parties believe a change in leadership is necessary to build on that success and achieve our long-term sporting goals."
Players were informed of the news on Monday after González was fired on Sunday, sources told ESPN.
Washington lost 2-1 to the Kansas City Current at Audi Field on Saturday in the NWSL Championship.
A source with knowledge of the Spirit's thinking said Saturday's loss was not the driving force in the team's decision, and that the Spirit felt a change was needed to move the team forward.
Washington's announcement on Monday stated that the team and González had "mutually agreed to part ways," and it included a statement from González.
"I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together at the Washington Spirit and grateful to the players, staff, ownership and supporters for their commitment and support throughout my time here," González said in a statement. "It has been an honor to lead this group, and I'm especially proud of the resilience and character the team has shown."
González joined the Spirit in early 2024 to serve as interim coach ahead of the arrival of Jonatan Giráldez, who left FC Barcelona to become the Spirit's head coach that year.
Washington finished second in the 2024 regular season and runners-up in the playoffs, losing to the Orlando Pride in the 2024 NWSL Championship.
Giráldez left the Spirit midway through the 2025 season to become head coach of OL Lyonnes, which has the same owner, Michelle Kang. González then became head coach of the team and guided the Spirit to another second-place finish in 2025 before losing to Gotham FC in the NWSL Championship.
This year was González's only full year as head coach. Washington finished the regular season in third place before losing Saturday's NWSL Championship on home soil against Kansas City.
Carter joined the Spirit late last year after serving as the architect of Orlando's run to the 2024 NWSL Shield and NWSL Championship.
The team said that "a comprehensive search" is underway for its next head coach.

items.title: Sources: Man Utd to appeal Yoro red card against Liverpool
items.summary:
Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, sources have told ESPN.
Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield on Sunday after a challenge on Alexander Isak.
The Frenchman was deemed to have denied
items.text:
Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, sources have told ESPN.
Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield on Sunday after a challenge on Alexander Isak.
The Frenchman was deemed to have denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity by referee Michael Oliver, a view backed up by VAR.
United head coach Mauricio Pochettino questioned the decision in his post-match news conference. He also compared the incident to a similar situation involving Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area which was not deemed to be a foul.
Sources have told ESPN that United's view is that Isak's heavy touch meant Senne Lammens would have gathered the ball before the striker had the chance to shoot.
Club bosses have informed the FA they will appeal the red card.
United conceded immediately after Yoro was sent off with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.
- Man United need big January transfer spend to avoid Premier League relegation
- Mauricio Pochettino gets reality check as Liverpool ruin his Man United debut
- Bruno Fernandes disputes Leny Yoro red card in Liverpool's rout of Man United
Liverpool went on to win 4-0 to hand Pochettino a heavy defeat in his first game since taking over from Michael Carrick.
The result leaves United 19th in the table and mired in relegation trouble after 11 games of the season.
What did Pochettino, Fernandes say about Yoro's red card?
Pochettino's perspective on the Yoro incident was: "I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control. The centre-back [Yoro] was running with him, Isak saw the control wasn't good and it is normal you delay, you stop to run, in that moment Yoro came from the back, and it is like a touch like this and you go down."
United midfielder Bruno Fernandes told BBC Sport: "I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.
"I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.
"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."
Kobbie Mainoo's verdict was: "I feel like the game was killed early with a decision by the referee that I don't think can be a red card.
"The ball is already with the keeper when he's gone down, two players running at full speed. I mean, it's impossible to be a red, but it is what it is.
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola disagreed, saying: "I think it's a situation where [Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper."

items.text:
Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan has been selected as the MLS Young Player of the Year for his breakthrough performance as a 17-year-old.
The award honors the top player who was born Jan. 1, 2004 or later. Sullivan is the youngest player ever to win the award.
Red Bull New York had the runner-up and third-place finishers in the voting. Julian Hall finished second and Adri Mehmeti was third.
Sullivan had nine goals and 14 assists over 28 games in his first MLS season as a full-time player. He had either a goal or an assist in 10 straight matches, the longest such streak by a teenager in MLS history.
Sullivan was called up to the United States men's national team in September and became the second-youngest player in U.S. history to start a match.
MLS players vote on this award along with club technical staff and media.

items.text:
Ann-Katrin Berger, the National Women's Soccer League's Goalkeeper of the Year this season, has joined German club Union Berlin as a free agent after three seasons with Gotham FC.
Gotham acquired the Germany national team keeper from Chelsea in 2024 for an undisclosed transfer fee. She started in all 73 regular-season matches she played with Gotham, with 29 shutouts.
During her time with the team, Gotham won the 2025 NWSL Championship, the 2026 NWSL Shield for best record and the 2024-25 CONCACAF Champions Cup.
"Ann has been instrumental in the success we've achieved over the past three seasons, and her impact on this club extends well beyond her performances in goal," Yael Averbuch West, Gotham's president of soccer operations, said in a statement. "Her consistency and ability to deliver in the biggest moments helped shape a championship-winning team."
Berger had 11 shutouts this season, making her the NWSL's first goalkeeper with at least 10 clean sheets in back-to-back seasons. She also won the league's goalkeeper of the year in the 2024 season.
Berger was goalkeeper for the German team that won the bronze medal at the Paris Olympics. She was also in goal when Germany reached the semifinals of the 2025 European Championship.
Berger, 36, will join Union Berlin in January, the Bundesliga club said.
"Union have courted me intensively and over a long period of time, which I really appreciate," Berger said in a statement released by Union Berlin.
"The path the club has taken in recent years is remarkable. I would like to use my experience to help drive this ambitious team forward. After so many years abroad, I'm really looking forward to returning to the Bundesliga. My thanks go to Gotham FC for a wonderful and successful time."

items.text:
Dad who discovered daughter's murder on Facebook feels ignored by South African police
- Published
Tuku Nkosiyaphantsi found out his daughter had been killed from a post on Facebook.
It was August and he hadn't been able to reach 27-year-old Okuhle for days, although it wasn't unusual for her to drop out of contact from time to time.
Then one Saturday, two of Tuku's neighbours called him to say that they had seen that Okuhle had been reported missing by police on Facebook. They had also seen a photo of what appeared to be Okuhle injured.
"When I looked at this photo, I saw that the person in it was dead, and when I looked closer I realised it was Okuhle," says Tuku, 50.
After seeing the image, Tuku phoned a police officer he knew. The policeman confirmed the woman in the picture had been killed and her body dumped near a river in Kokstad, an agricultural hub in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province, in the east of the country.
But because the morgue was closed for the weekend, it wasn't until Monday morning that Tuku was able to identify Okuhle's body.
When he did, Tuku saw she had been mutilated and her face badly beaten.
"It was very painful, so much that I cannot accept it."
Okuhle had two children, aged nine and three, and was a civil engineering student.
She is among 581 women who were killed in the country between July and September, according to the South African Police Service.
Overall, there were 5,590 murders - 204 fewer than in the same period last year.
It is the first time police have broken down murders by gender, so it is unclear whether the number of women killed is an increase or decrease on previous years.
There has been a renewed national outcry this year about the scale of violence against women after the partially naked and bruised bodies of 12 women were found dumped in public areas in Ekurhuleni, a district to the east of Johannesburg, this summer.
South Africa has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence and femicide - the intentional killing of a woman or girl - in the world.
Am I Next? Fear and Survival in South Africa
The BBC World Service visits communities struggling to confront widespread violence against women
In response to this summer's killings, President Cyril Ramaphosa promised safety audits across every municipality to identify and address dangerous spaces for women, as well as an increased police presence in the worst-affected areas.
But in places like Kokstad and Kempton Park, both in Ekurhuleni, the BBC World Service saw people taking the protection of women into their own hands.
For Tuku, that means investigating his daughter's killing himself.
Months after she was killed, he says no-one has been arrested.
"It was just silent after we buried Okuhle - there was nothing at all. I so wish the police would stand up and investigate."
He believes police failed to review CCTV footage from a local government building in the town that may have shown who his daughter was with on the day she disappeared. The footage is wiped every seven days, he says.
The BBC approached the South African Police Service for comment but at the time of publication, no response had been received.
The police service has previously acknowledged shortcomings in its overall response to gender-based violence and femicide, adding that it was continuing to invest in addressing these challenges. Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has said there needs to be "greater efforts" to prevent violence against women and children.
According to a 2024 report by the South African Medical Research Council, the number of unsolved cases of femicide was growing.
This year, Amnesty International said South Africa's police service was "under-resourced, poorly equipped, and insufficiently trained to respond effectively and sensitively to gender-based violence".
Tuku says he is now searching for CCTV footage and seeking out people who knew his daughter in the hope of finding leads.
Despite Ramaphosa's promises, he has little faith anything will change.
"I listened to Ramaphosa. The government acts only when something happened. We in Kokstad, we feel like we are ignored and unseen. The government does not care for us."
Asked earlier this month by the BBC what progress South Africa had made to keep women safe, Ramaphosa said the government would be allocating extra money in February's budget to deal with gender-based violence.
Speaking as he cast his vote in local elections, Ramaphosa added that the government had increased police numbers in the last three years "and we will continue to do so, so that there can be more visible policing".
Okuhle is not the only woman to be killed this year in Kokstad.
Between January and October this year, the bodies of five women and three very young children were found in the town, with arrests only taking place in two of the cases.
In response, this summer, the community set up street patrols and a curfew for women and children.
Since June, children have been told to be indoors by sunset and women by 21:00.
Kamvalethu Cetywayo, 34, from a local neighbourhood watch group, leads a group of around 15 men who patrol crime hotspots in the town at night, including areas where bodies have been found or trouble has been reported to them.
The patrols tend to take place between Thursday and Sunday because this is when people drink alcohol most heavily, says Kamvalethu.
Most of the patrollers carry sticks, whips and torches, but Kamvalethu has a licensed gun. He says the group will call police when they need back-up.
Asked how he feels about restricting the freedoms of women and children, Kamvalethu says the curfew helps keep them safe, is voluntary, and a temporary measure until police arrest the killers.
"With the resolution we made with the community, we get to assist them with this, but if people are refusing there's nothing we can do."
Even so, not all victims are attacked at night or on the streets.
Kgothatso Mojela was kidnapped on her way to work in 2018 in Kempto

items.text:
Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
- Published
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.
Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.
Konstantinos Tzolakis (Hull City): If you watched the Brighton game and wondered how on earth Hull won it was because Konstantinos Tzolakis was in goal. An unbelievable performance with five or six top-class saves. Big moments, big personality, he has stepped up every time. He's been one of the players of the season - I know it's a bit too early to crown people but if it stopped now he has to be goalkeeper of the season.
James Hill (Bournemouth): He backed up getting into the England squad. Sometimes when people get called up they start to get above their stations but he didn't do that at all. He was in a really good state of form. A cheeky assist as well but defensively solid. He has been in my team a few times now - a centre-half who does his job without complaining.
Malick Thiaw (Newcastle): He divides opinion but he played really well and got his goal.
Keane Lewis-Potter (Brentford): Two goals against Everton and that was before the sending-off of James Tarkowski. Performed well again. Sneaky bargain buy of the century to be honest.
Noah Okafor (Leeds): Two goals again. Leeds battered Chelsea and made them look unbelievably average. Nobody has been talking about how sneaky good Leeds have been, some really big performances this season.
Jack Rudoni (Coventry): Two assists in a must-win game against Crystal Palace. He stepped up big, fair play to him.
Elliott Anderson (Manchester City): The only person who actually showed a pulse in this game. He got a goal and showed pace and showed he wanted to be there. He tried his best to win a game of football.
Luca Williams-Barnett (Tottenham): Young man, a with goal and an assist. He just gave Spurs a spark we haven't seen for probably six or seven years now. He gave them that spark instantly and fair play to De Zerbi for putting him in. All the money spent, who knew it would be a home-grown talent in their youth team who would step up and really get the Spurs fans excited.
Florian Wirtz (Liverpool): Unbelievable performance. He has had a bit of a purple patch since Jurgen Klopp has taken over Germany. Did really well in terms of finding the gaps, drifting between players and finding through balls and now adding goals. Now we are seeing the player we saw in Germany and I am buzzing for him.
Oli McBurnie (Hull City): The man of the moment. He works really hard, he does everything for the team to make sure they are there. He is solid defensively but then he gets two shots and two goals. Top performance from him.
Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool): He made Diogo Dalot look like he'd never played a game before, not the fact he has played over 250 games for Manchester United and has gone to World Cups with Portugal and made him look childish, Ran him every time and twisted him inside out and got his goal.
Frank Lampard (Coventry): In the biggest game of the season so far for him he made sure he got the job done. Big win. No new-manager bounce for Palace as Lampard gets the job done and he made some big calls.

- Published
It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski.

But that run came
items.text:
Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
- Published
It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski.
Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record.
But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate.
His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history.
The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year.
Tarkowski's dismissal proved a big talking point during and after the match, with opinions split on whether he should have gone. Even Moyes wasn't sure.
He told BBC Match of the Day: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that."
Why did Tarkowski get sent off?
So what exactly happened?
Just 15 minutes after Keane Lewis-Potter scored his second deflected strike of the evening, Everton skipper Tarkowski thundered into a challenge on Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk.
He won the ball but also followed through with the challenge forcefully. Initially, referee Craig Pawson deemed a foul and a yellow card was enough.
But, after an intervention from the video assistant referee (VAR) and studying the replay, Pawson changed the yellow for a red.
The Premier League match centre said on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play.
"VAR: 'Point of contact is on the shin. He's got speed and intensity. Studs are high.'
"REF: 'After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card - and a red card.'"
'Game's gone' or '100% red'? Experts are split
Referees are asked to take into account several considerations for what counts as serious foul play including the speed of the challenge, its intensity, force and what degree of control there was.
But, as always, there was plenty of debate about whether it was the correct decision.
BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, said: "Really not sure about this as a VAR red card.
"Yes, Tarkowski absolutely ticks the boxes for speed and intensity and leading high with studs showing.
"But the question marks are that Tarkowski made only small contact and didn't have a straight leg when he did so.
"Maybe his reputation played a part? Remember, he wrongly escaped a VAR red card against Liverpool for a challenge, which was along the same lines. He won the ball and then followed through into Alexis Mac Allister. Thought that was a far stronger challenge."
BBC Radio 5 Live's - and former Blackburn Rovers striker - Chris Sutton, said on X: "Come on that's not a red… the game's gone."
Former Arsenal striker Alan Smith agreed the decision was harsh. He told Sky Sports: "Ten years ago we wouldn't have looked at it once and now we still [frame] it on the follow-through. I just can't see it.
"Only Tarkowski knows if he wanted to leave it high or if it was natural. The follow-through was just natural momentum.
"There's a bit of anger in there from Tarkowski and it's a little high but only he knows if he wanted to leave a little more on Yarmoliuk there."
Opinion was far from unanimous though, with both pundits in the Sky Sports studio adamant it was a clear red.
Former Liverpool centre-back Jamie Carragher said: "It's a red card. Tarkowski has got previous for tackles like that. He is a 90s defender, he tackles like that.
"He follows through with such force, it is excessive. You want to give him the benefit of the doubt but it's a red card."
He added: "You could argue was it a big enough mistake for VAR to get involved but I think we are splitting hairs. He doesn't need to do this."
While ex-Totenham defender Toby Alderweireld added: "It's a red card, he knows what he is doing. 100%."
'Never a red' or a 'clear' sending off - what you thought
Josh, Sheffield: Never a red for Tarkowski and I'm a Liverpool fan. What's he meant to do? Stop momentum. It's a good tackle and the player runs into the natural follow through
Robin, Essex: Another game ruined by VAR! Not straight leg tackle you can surely see he turned his foot around. Poor!
Rob, Manchester: These sorts of VAR decisions are making me turn off football. Why pay all that money to watch arbitrary decisions impact the game?
Lee: It is a sad day when a good tackle gets a player sent off. You slow anything down and dissect it you can find wrongs. Yellow was a bit much and the red ridiculous, we need ex players in the VAR decisions too.
Max, Oldham: What a load of nonsense the red card is. Tarkowski can't stop his momentum. VAR has ruined another game, plus what is the ref doing? He had a chance to stick with the yellow card. Another case of an official who has never played the game.
Paul, St Asaph: Tarkowski has got away with that same foul a few times. Do think he's the type of player to leave one in on purpose.
Anon: Yes it's a red - Tarkowski knows what he's doing, it's frustration and wanting to leave a bit on the player.
Chris, Chelmsford: He does it all the time at the borderline but about time he got one.
Woody, London: Lack of refinement masked as passion, classic Tarkowski tackle there… glad to see him off.
George, Birmingham: Studs up in a tackle, he has to go. A clear red card for me.

items.title: Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
items.summary:
Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
For more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
items.text:
Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
For more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange.
Stalwart now implements the protocols that Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover. Outlook, Apple Mail and the mail apps on phones and tablets connect to Stalwart as they would to an Exchange server, with mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes in one account. Users type their email address and password, Autodiscover does the rest, and they keep working in the client they already know.
Exchange support is part of the open source Community edition, under the AGPL.
Exchange on premises in 2026
Section titled “Exchange on premises in 2026”
Before going into what Stalwart now does, it is worth looking at where self-hosted Exchange stands today, because it explains why so many organisations are looking for a way out.
Microsoft has not announced the end of Exchange Server. On paper, on-premises Exchange still exists. In practice, every road Microsoft is building leads to Exchange Online:
- Exchange 2016 and 2019 are out of support. Both reached end of support on 14 October 2025. Microsoft sold a paid Extended Security Update programme for a while, and according to press reports of an Exchange team statement, it ended in October 2026 with no further extension. Servers still running those versions receive no fixes of any kind.
- No new features. Exchange Server Subscription Edition (SE) is now the only supported on-premises Exchange, and there will be no more major versions after it. SE does not receive the features developed for the cloud. Even its first cumulative update has slipped from late 2025 to an undetermined date in 2026.
- The new Outlook does not support it. Microsoft’s own documentation for the new Outlook for Windows says it plainly: “On-premises Exchange accounts aren’t supported.”
- The APIs are moving to the cloud. New functionality ships only on Microsoft Graph, a cloud API. Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online started being switched off in October 2026 and will be gone entirely in April 2027.
None of these steps forces anyone to move on its own. Together, they leave an Exchange administrator with a shrinking set of choices: keep running a server that will not grow, or move the organisation’s mail into Microsoft’s cloud.
For many organisations the second option is not acceptable. Email is the record of a company’s contracts, negotiations, legal advice, HR matters and customer data. Placing it with a US provider means placing it within reach of US law, including the CLOUD Act, which allows US authorities to compel American providers to hand over data they control wherever it is stored. Public administrations, healthcare providers, law firms, defence contractors and many European companies cannot accept that, or no longer want to. Data sovereignty means that you decide where your data lives, under which jurisdiction, and who can read it. A mail service in someone else’s cloud cannot offer that, and an on-premises server whose vendor is steering its customers toward that cloud offers less of it every year.
Outlook without Exchange
Section titled “Outlook without Exchange”
The obstacle to leaving Exchange has rarely been the server. It has been the client.
Many people have spent their whole working life in Outlook. They have years of muscle memory in it: their folder layout, their rules, their calendar views, their shared mailboxes, the way they book meeting rooms. Many organisations also have workflows built around it, such as delegated calendars managed by an assistant. Replacing Exchange with a standard IMAP and CalDAV server has always meant telling every one of those users to switch to a different mail client, or to reconfigure Outlook into a reduced IMAP mode where calendars and contacts no longer sync. For a migration project, that is often where the plan dies.
With Stalwart 1.2.0 the users do not need to change anything. The administrator moves the mailboxes and points the DNS records at Stalwart, and users connect with the same Outlook they used before.
Supported protocols and clients
Section titled “Supported protocols and clients”
Stalwart implements the following Microsoft protocols, all served on the same HTTPS port as JMAP and the WebUI:
- MAPI over HTTP (EMSMDB and NSPI), the native protocol of classic Outlook for Windows, in both cached and online mode. It covers mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes, incremental synchronisation, the global address list and the offline address book, delegate access, shared mailboxes, rules, junk email settings, reminders, search folders and read receipts.
- Exchange Web Services, schema versions Exchange 2010 SP2 to Exchange 2016: mail, calendars, contacts, tasks, folders, sharing and delegates, free/busy, inbox rules, out of office, name resolution, distribution lists, and streaming and pull notifications.
- Exchange ActiveSync 14.1 and 16.1: mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes, with push through Ping, meeting responses, search and out of office.
- Autodiscover in its POX, SOAP and JSON dialects, so clients configure themselves from an email address and a password.
That set of protocols is what the following clients use to talk to an Exchange server, and they can connect to Stalwart the same way:
- Classic Outlook for Windows (Outlook 2016 and later, including Microsoft 365 Apps), over MAPI over HTTP and EWS.
- Outlook for Mac, over EWS.
- Apple Mail, Calendar and Contacts on macOS, through an Exchange account over EWS.
- Mail, Calendar and Contacts on iPhone and iPad, through an Exchange account over ActiveSync.
- Android mail apps with Exchange account support, such as Gmail, Samsung Email and Nine, over ActiveSync.

LPGA Tour Q-Series: Megan Khang secures tour card for 2027 as Megha Ganne wins final qualifying stage
The top-25 finishers and ties at the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage have been awarded LPGA Tour status for 2027; Megha Ganne won the event outright, while Megan Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is one of 27 players to claim a tour card for next season
Monday 23 November 2026 23:16, UK
Megha Ganne won the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage as 27 tour cards were claimed for the 2027 season, with five-time USA Solheim Cup team member Megan Khang among those successful.
Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is returning to the LPGA Tour, on which she's made 259 starts since 2016, winning the 2023 CPKC Women's Open.
The top-25 finishers and ties at the conclusion of the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying were awarded LPGA Tour status for next year.
American Ganne won the final stage outright on 23 under, one shot clear of Shannon Tan and Julia Gregg in a tie for second. Min Sun7 Kim was fourth on 21 under and Xiaowen Yin one further back in fifth.
Ganne, the 2025 US Amateur champion, had actually already secured her 2027 LPGA Tour status by entering the week by finishing 11-15 on the Epson Tour.
Gregg, who finished in a share of second, has never previously had a start on the LPGA Tour.
"It feels unreal," the 25-year-old American said after clinching her place. "It's been my dream since I was four years old to play on the LPGA and now that I finally did it."
What's next in women's golf?
The WTGL season continues on Wednesday when Lottie Woad's Boston Common chase their first win of the campaign against Charley Hull's Atlanta Drive GC. Live coverage begins on Wednesday from 1am on Sky Sports Golf.

After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.
Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.
News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”
But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.
The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.
The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.
The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.
Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. items.text:
After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO.
And then… Huang was back.
In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation.
Follow along below for all of the latest updates.
- Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. - Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened. Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now. Read Article >
- Here’s Trump discussing the Jensen Huang situation on TV for 10 minutes. Trump did the TV circuit this morning to talk up how involved he was in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday. He said on CNBC that he spoke to Nvidia’s board, adding, “I convinced them.”
- Jensen Huang says he’ll be a ‘better CEO’ as staff applauds his return Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s office as CEO today to a crowd of applauding employees who stood and filmed the cofounder’s first moments back. “Thank you all for the second chances. I’m gonna be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang said, as shown in a video of his return. Read Article >
- How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago cofounded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.” Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman — Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed — to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. Read Article >
- Jensen Huang has already come back to Nvidia’s offices. Employees applauded for his return.
- White House brags that Trump was ‘totally involved’ in getting Jensen reinstated It sure looked like President Donald Trump played a role in Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO — and now the White House is making sure everyone knows he was. “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement, which was first reported by Semafor. “We have to protect our geniuses.” Trump later went on CNBC with a similar statement. “We have to protect our geniuses,” he said on the air. But he did nothing wrong.” Read Article >

items.summary: It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received
items.text:
It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances.
Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk would not have been a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player? The reality is Tarkowski’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles, meaning there was always likely to come a time when his luck ran out.
Everton, whose passive performance denied them the chance to go fifth, should not bother complaining about Matthew Donohue’s intervention from Stockley Park after Tarkowski went in on Yarmoliuk with his studs raised late in the first half. It was the defender’s first red since he was playing for Brentford in the Championship and it had no great bearing on the result. Brentford led 2-0 before their former player went off, Keane Lewis-Potter’s third and fourth goals of the season putting them in control, and dominated from start to finish.
Keith Andrews, a young coach who will have done something right if he comes close to matching Moyes’s longevity, revelled in his side moving sixth thanks to an outstanding display. Moyes has been around long enough to know the top flight has rarely been this open but on this evidence Brentford look likelier than Everton to upset the established order. It was a drubbing, a cracking third from Vitaly Janelt followed by Fábio Carvalho making it 4-0 in added time, and made clear that Brentford have the tools to challenge for European qualification.
With Igor Thiago unavailable after his controversial red card against Brighton it fell to Callum Wilson to lead the line for Brentford. Everton were unsettled by Wilson’s movement and were strangely muted. They sat in a low block but were not compact, were careless in possession and did not deal with Brentford’s wing play and midfield interchanges.
Jaidon Anthony, Mikkel Damsgaard and Michael Kayode had chances before Everton cracked. They were caught out by a long ball down the left and were undone when a poor clearing header led to a moment of brilliance from Anthony, the winger’s cushioned touch with the outside of his right foot running for Lewis-Potter to beat Jordan Pickford thanks to a deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite.
Brentford love to make the most of Lewis-Potter’s attacking instincts after converting him into a left-back. He joined as a winger and his runs are always a threat but Everton did not pay close enough attention. They were abysmal in the first half and faced more pressure when Vitaliy Mykolenko conceded a free-kick after losing Dango Ouattara. Damsgaard crossed, Everton were all at sea and Lewis-Potter scored via another deflection, this time off Thierno Barry.
Everton were dour. They sought a lifeline through Harrison Armstrong, Caiomhín Kelleher tipping the midfielder’s shot over, but composure eluded them. Tarkowski, seemingly rattled by the barracking from the home crowd, was off after storming into a challenge Yarmoliuk. The initial call was a yellow but Tarkowski’s boot was high, the follow-through looked cynical and the force was excessive, convincing Craig Pawson to show a red after a VAR review.
“I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” Andrews said. Moyes was honest, admitting that Tarkowski’s boot was high. “I can see why the decision went against us,” Everton’s manager said.
Everton adjusted after going down to 10, Merlin Röhl going to right-back, and Thierno Barry’s header drew a superb save from Kelleher just before half-time. Brentford had to switch on. They were intense at the start of the second half and Ouattara nodded wide from Damsgaard’s cross.
Moyes had introduced Jack Grealish for Tyrique George. Yet Brentford recognised the threat and killed Everton off when Janelt used his left foot to belt a formidable shot past Pickford from 30 yards.
“We didn’t play well,” Moyes said. “It was really not like us. I’ve got no complaints with the players. They’ve done a brilliant job until now. Tonight’s performance was not excusable.”
Everton were outplayed on every metric. They were lucky Brentford waited so long to score a fourth, Carvalho coming on to round off the humiliation by bundling in a corner from close range.

Consequences are for the poors.
Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.
The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy
I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance.
Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.
In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia. In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it, several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive
What changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America.
Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “absolutely fine.”
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer, “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.
Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally
One thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing. That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade. He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI, a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?
Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. For every field, circuits for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, and for the permanent outside characteristic 2, need more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates for all large m. The same holds for approximating circuits. So VP is a proper subset of VNP, and VNP is not contained in the closure of VP. This does not settle P vs NP.
The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model. This folder holds the paper and its Lean 4 formalization. Both were written by AI models, and no human mathematician has checked the proof.
Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions.
paper.pdf: VP ≠ VNP over every field, by Claude (Anthropic). The full proof is its appendix.
1. Read the statement. Statement.lean states all of the above and imports only Mathlib. Lean checks the proofs, but no machine checks that this file says what is claimed. Appendix Q of paper.pdf lists the Lean counterparts of the numbered statements (Table 3) and says where they differ.
2. Check the proofs. With elan installed, in this folder:
lake exe cache get
lake build
lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean
The build prints sorry warnings from Challenge.lean only, which states the theorems without proofs for the fuller check. The last command should name no axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
The fuller check is the one this repository's CI runs, bash ../.github/scripts/comparator-check.sh (Linux): Comparator compares the statements with Challenge.lean and re-checks the proofs with a second, independently written kernel, nanoda.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
items.summary:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is th
items.text:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.
The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.
Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.
Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

items.summary:
AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.
Now, the company has r
items.text:
AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.
Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.
Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.
“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.
The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading launches like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.
The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a new level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.
Currently, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.
Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.
Supertake’s users’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.
For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.
Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.
“We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”
“I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he says.
Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.
“We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being said, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.
To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team says it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.
“We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” says Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”
Access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders said they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.
Mignano, meanwhile, says he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.
With the new funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. items.text:
Henry Patten ends partnership with Harri Heliovaara to team up with fellow Briton Neal Skupski
Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara were crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after winning Wimbledon for a second time in July; the pair have won three Grand Slam doubles titles together but will go their separate ways in 2027
Monday 23 November 2026 22:29, UK
Henry Patten has ended his world No 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion in favour of teaming up with British compatriot Neal Skupski for 2027.
Patten and Heliovaara celebrated being crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after they claimed a second Wimbledon success together back in July.
However, in a post on Heliovaara's blog, the Finnish player revealed Patten phoned him on Friday to say their three-time Grand Slam-winning partnership was over - despite a previous agreement they would continue.
"After the trip to Turin, I didn't even have time to get into the holiday mood when the weekend took a rather unexpected turn," Heliovaara said on his own blog website. "Henry completely unexpectedly announced that he had changed his mind about next year.
"I picked up the kids from daycare on Friday afternoon and we were just opening presents when I got a call from Henry. Without going into too much detail, the message was clear.
"He didn't want to play together again next year, even though we had agreed to do so during the fall. The announcement came as completely as it could come and I couldn't help but listen with my mouth open in horror and say that I don't agree at all.
"I'm unlikely to ever fully understand what and why this ultimately happened.
"The emotional scale in my head was quite violent at first, a shocking situation in any case.
"The two-and-a-half years with Henry have been by far the best time of my career, for which I am eternally grateful to him, but now the main feeling was heavy disappointment and even anger."
Heliovaara confirmed in his blog that he would team up with another British player Julian Cash, while Patten is set to partner Skupski in 2027.
